A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RepLoRA work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and section relocation.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original RepLoRA experiments across language, image, video, and multimodal tasks, including sample-efficiency and reparameterization analyses.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendix C retain these original experiments and analyses, with additional DoRA comparison results.

M1.justification: Both versions generate query/value low-rank matrices through two-layer MLPs with shared inputs and separate output heads, use diagonal input matrices, and discard the MLPs after training. The newly specified sigmoid activation is additional documentation, not an established method change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same eight commonsense tasks, VTAB-1K, five FGVC datasets, SSv2/HMDB51, and eight image/video-text tasks. The subsampled FGVC scenarios are also retained; no dataset or task coverage is added.

E2.justification: DoRA becomes an evaluated comparator for LLaMA-7B/13B commonsense reasoning, FGVC, and VL-BART image/video-text tasks in Tables 1, 2, 5, and 6. It was previously only cited. Other comparator memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported splits, metrics, backbones, training settings, and hyperparameters in Tables 7–9 are unchanged. FGVC subsampling still uses the same fractions and inverse-fraction epoch scaling. No revised evaluation protocol is reported for the retained experiments.

E4.justification: The FGVC sample-efficiency analysis and cross-domain linear-versus-nonlinear comparisons are retained with the same evidence. Appendix D becomes Appendix C; this relocation and Figure 4's rearrangement introduce no new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, error bars, or significance tests. The additional DoRA rows retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries in all 16 tables remain unchanged. New DoRA results include average accuracies of 78.4/81.5 for LLaMA-7B/13B and 87.2 for FGVC. Table 1 also newly shows DoRA exceeding RepLoRA on HellaSwag: 87.2 versus 85.2 and 92.4 versus 91.1.

T1.justification: Section 5.2 adds an argument that distinct query/value projections sharing A can be accommodated without changing the convergence analysis. Appendix A contains limited derivation edits, including revised Fatou steps and an expanded logarithmic bound in A.4. The three rate theorems and relocated activation assumptions are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same MoE interpretation, exponential-to-polynomial sample-complexity claim, RepLoRA proposal, and empirical superiority claims. The headline claims of up to 40% improvement and matching LoRA with 30% of training data are unchanged.

C2.justification: V1 acknowledges that equating query/value low-rank matrices simplifies the theory relative to practice. V2 additionally argues that separate projections sharing an input merely complicate the analysis and treats the equality restriction as without loss of generality. This extends the stated applicability interpretation without a new general-case proof.

D1.justification: V1 specifies two-layer nonlinear networks with hidden dimension 64. V2 Appendix C.2 additionally identifies sigmoid activation functions for all settings. The other implementation and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds FuseMoE, softmax-gated multinomial logistic MoE theory, and cosine-router research, while removing the discussion of Ho et al. (2022) on Gaussian MoE. The overall positioning remains similar; moving related work into Section 2 is principally structural.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained, with local prose revisions and proof streamlining. Related work moves from Appendix B to Section 2, references precede the supplement, and activation assumptions move to Appendix A.3. V2 also updates affiliations and adds impact and acknowledgement paragraphs.

P2.justification: V2 comprehensively reformats the main text into a two-column conference layout, resizing and relocating figures and tables. Tables 1, 2, 5, and 6 gain DoRA rows, and Figure 4 changes from a 2–1–2 panel arrangement to 3–2. The four figures and sixteen tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The added DoRA comparisons provide a more informative assessment against another LoRA variant, including cases where RepLoRA does not lead. Specifying sigmoid activations modestly improves reproducibility. These gains are limited: existing results and theoretical guarantees remain unchanged, and the new generalization assertion lacks a corresponding general-case proof.
